title: Foundations: SPORT & FITT

meta_desc: GCSE PE Principles of Training foundations: SPORT, FITT and progressive overload.

concepts.def: Training must match the demands of the sport.
Gradually increasing the difficulty of training.
Working harder than usual to force adaptation.
Fitness loss when training stops — use it or lose it.
Boredom from repetitive training — keep it varied.
Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type — ways to overload.

walkthroughs.body_html:
SPORT:

  • Specificity — match training to sport.
  • Progression — increase load step by step.
  • Overload — push past comfort zone.
  • Reversibility — gains lost if you stop.
  • Tedium — vary training to stay motivated.

FITT tells you HOW to overload:

  • Frequency — how often (e.g. 3 → 4 sessions/week).
  • Intensity — how hard (heavier weight, higher HR).
  • Time — how long (longer runs).
  • Type — what activity (vary methods).
Stop training and gains reverse. Aerobic fitness drops noticeably after about 2 weeks; muscle strength after 3-4. Injuries make this a real risk — rehab keeps adaptations going where possible.
